title: Headwise reprojection + fallback path to reduce mixed-precision decode overhead
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: Mixed INT8/FP8 execution on the decode path incurs per-head dequant/reproject costs and head-level numeric instability that forces expensive FP fallbacks. On streaming decode this amplifies p99 latency and increases per-token cost. Goal: implement a headwise reprojection + attenuation path that avoids a full per-token dequant whenever head activations are numerically stable, while providing a fast, low-overhead fallback to per-head FP8 compute when instability or accuracy regressions are detected. Approach: (1) Add a lightweight head stability scorer computed from head statistics during prefill and early decode tokens; (2) Introduce a reprojection kernel that transforms packed INT8 attention outputs into a compensated FP8 intermediate with an attenuation factor to bound variance; this kernel is optimized for contiguous head slices and fused into the post-attention epilogue; (3) Implement a kernel selector heuristic that prefers the reprojection path for heads with stability_score >= threshold and switches to per-head FP8 kernels otherwise; (4) Extend the runtime scheduler to treat reprojection heads as fast paths during microbatching and to prioritize their placement on lanes with lower memory copy overhead; (5) Add telemetry (head_stability_score, reprojection_hits, reprojection_fallback_rate, reprojection_latency_us) and an evaluation harness to correlate reprojection usage with downstream perplexity/quality metrics. Trade-offs and rationale: reprojection reduces per-token compute and avoids costly rounding/alloc churn, but introduces a subtle risk of small numeric drift; we mitigate this by conservative thresholds, A/B quality checks on a held-out prompt set, and a gradual canary rollout. Performance target: decrease decode p99 latency by 6-12% on 1k token streaming workloads and reduce per-token GPU cycles by ~4-7% for workloads with >60% stable heads. Acceptance criteria: (a) reprojection kernel is implemented and selected by the kernel selector for stable heads; (b) fallback path reliably triggers on instability with end-to-end correctness preserved; (c) telemetry shows reprojection_hits > 50% for targeted workloads in canary; (d) A/B eval shows no >0.5% degradation in our prompt set metrics; (e) rollout guide and kill-switch implemented. Rollout plan: dev-feature branch -> internal perf harness -> canary on dedicated cluster (10%) with realtime quality checks -> ramp to 100% in runtime-1.23 if stable. Docs/Artifacts: design doc (Confluence), microbench scripts, and perf dashboards linked below.
comments: 2026-02-22: Spike completed. Proved head stability score (variance of scaled matmul outputs over first 8 decode tokens) correlates with numeric divergence in int8->fp8 reprojections.
2026-02-28: Prototype reprojection kernel landed in branch feat/reproj-kernel. Microbench shows 20-30% lower kernel time vs naive int8->fp8 cast+copy for contiguous head slices.
2026-03-03: Kernel selector integration finished; added gating flag runtime.reprojection.enabled. Need to finalize threshold heuristic and add telemetry counters.
2026-03-05: Design review feedback from Marco: add attenuation multiplier cap and explicit per-model calibration step. Updated design doc.
2026-03-09: QA found an instability with variable head widths on older model variants; added normalization path and unit tests. Assigned follow-up to ENG-672501.

2026-03-12: Canary started on dedicated cluster (10% traffic). Early telemetry: reprojection_hits 58%, reprojection_fallback_rate 1.2%, p99 latency improvement ~7% on target workload. Monitoring dashboard link in Links below. Next: expand prompt set quality checks and prepare rollback playbook.
Follow-ups after rollout: collect long-tail prompts, tune thresholds per-model, and consider per-customer opt-in for aggressive thresholds.
